correctness.rationale: Three disjoint paths and left/right row boundary give an exact cut classification. A coordinatewise feasible-region proof establishes an all-pairs Manhattan slide metric; optimization of a convex endpoint eccentricity formula yields the sharp radius and diameter. Two standalone independently constructed graph methods exhaustively check up to nine and 24 columns, respectively, including all-pairs shortest paths. The proof, not bounded runs, establishes every n>=3.

value.rationale: A natural planar width-three network has a complete quantified minimum-cut configuration space and exact rearrangement cost without non-minimum intermediate states. The 9(n-2) state law, 16n-36 edges, all-pairs metric, radius and diameter 3n-5 form a motivated all-length benchmark for optimum-preserving network separation, going beyond generic algorithmic feasibility. Limitations to these terminal placements are explicit.
